role: EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY of the four changed dispatchers. Vendored via the newly-flattened phoenix-nft-staking submodule; remapping `phoenix-nft-staking/=lib/phoenix-nft-staking/src/`. NOT first-party to yield-claim-nft — profiled here only to fix the semantics downstream agents must assume.

collectNudgeSemantics.signature: collectNudge(address recipientBatchMinter, address token, uint256 amount)
orderOfOperations: 2. _settle(s, recipientBatchMinter, token)  -- pays the accrued-so-far buffer OUT to the batchMinter (outbound safeTransfer). Happens BEFORE the zero-amount check.
4. safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount)  -- pulls EXACTLY `amount` from the donor's allowance
6. s.rewardPerSecond = s.buffer * 1e18 / s.duration   <-- FULL-WINDOW RATE RESET ON EVERY DEPOSIT
collectNudgeSemantics.whatItActuallyIs: A TIMING THROTTLE. It meters the RATE at which a donation becomes visible in the batchMinter's ERC20 balance. It places NO ceiling on how much value any single batchMint can capture: the batchMinter flushes with pullPendingStream and then snapshots its whole balance. If the buffer has had time to drain, one caller still captures the entire accrued amount in one transaction.
collectNudgeSemantics.asymptoticTail: Because step 6 resets the window to the FULL `duration` over the WHOLE (old + new) buffer on every deposit, a stream that receives regular donations never depletes -- each deposit re-stretches the residual over a fresh full window. The buffer approaches a steady state, and the per-second release fraction of the *residual* falls as donation cadence rises. This is the intended phlimbo `_updatePool` port (recompute-on-deposit-only; recompute is deliberately absent from `pullPendingStream` and from views).
collectNudgeSemantics.dustDirection: `_accrued` floors (integer division) and is capped at `buffer`. Floor dust stays in the buffer and streams later. Never over-pays; never transfers more than held.
collectNudgeSemantics.decimalNeutrality: PRECISION = 1e18 is an internal fixed-point multiplier that CANCELS (rate = buf*1e18/dur, accrued = rate*elapsed/1e18). All buffers and transfers are in the token's NATIVE units. 6-dp USDC and 18-dp tokens both work. It exists only to stop `buffer/duration` truncating to zero for small-decimal tokens over long windows.

otherEntryPoints.function: registerStream(address batchMinter, address token, uint256 duration)
otherEntryPoints.accessControl: onlyOwner (streamer owner -- a DIFFERENT owner from any yield-claim-nft dispatcher owner)
preconditions: IMultiTokenNudgeWhitelist(batchMinter).isNudgeToken(token) == true -- this call also reverts for any target that is not a MultiToken batchMinter, which is the structural type guard
otherEntryPoints.effect: settles at OLD rate, then s.duration = duration and rewardPerSecond = buffer*1e18/duration (full new window from now)

otherEntryPoints.accessControl: none; msg.sender IS the recipient key
otherEntryPoints.effect: settles accrued to msg.sender. Unregistered (duration==0) is a silent no-op, so BatchNFTMinterMultiToken can loop blindly over getNudgeTokens().

verifiedProperties.cei: _settle updates buffer/lastUpdate BEFORE its outbound transfer; collectNudge pulls funds before the rate recompute.
verifiedProperties.solvency: _accrued caps at s.buffer, so per-stream payout can never exceed that stream's buffer. There is NO cross-stream isolation check: all streams share one token balance, but since every buffer is only credited by an actual transferFrom of that same amount, sum(buffers) == held balance by construction.

callerAssumptionDivergences: Dispatcher NatSpec says the streamer means the batchMinter 'is paid over time rather than in a lump'. Correct for arrival RATE; it does NOT bound the total a single batchMint can take. Any downstream reasoning that treats the streamer as an anti-over-funding VALUE cap (cf. phoenix-nft-staking run-22 aggregate-nudge over-funding) is unsupported by this implementation.

There is NO owner rescue / sweep on NudgeStreamer. Buffers are addressable only by (batchMinter, token) and only drainable by that batchMinter calling pullPendingStream, or by a donor's collectNudge settling to it. If the batchMinter is ever REPLACED with a new address, the old pair's residual buffer has no recovery path.

The batchMinter's OWN `nudgeStreamer` field (BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer) is a SEPARATE, independently-set pointer from each dispatcher's `nudgeStreamer`. If they disagree (or the batchMinter's is address(0)), donations accumulate in the streamer and are never flushed into the pot -- funds sit undistributed until the batchMinter is re-pointed.

collectNudge's `_settle` fires an outbound ERC20 transfer to the batchMinter BEFORE the donor's transferFrom. With USDC/USDS (no transfer hooks) this is inert; with a hook-bearing token it would be an inbound-callback surface into an nonReentrant-guarded streamer, re-entered from inside the dispatcher's own nonReentrant dispatch.

batchMinterIntegrationFacts.flushSite: BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint step 3.5 -- loops the whole whitelist calling pullPendingStream(_nudgeTokens[i]) BEFORE _snapshotRewards.
batchMinterIntegrationFacts.consequence: Streamed funds settled at step 3.5 ARE counted in the pre-loop snapshot and paid to the CURRENT batcher. Donations generated by the same batch's own mint loop (step 7 -> dispatcher -> collectNudge) land AFTER the snapshot, so the 'donate forward' property survives the streamer change. Note that at step 3.5 and at the in-loop collectNudge the timestamp is identical, so the in-loop `_settle` accrues zero -- no self-refund leak.
